Knit a document under several cases and see which arms they choose

Source: R/rehearse.R
rehearse.Rd

Knits file once for each case, each in a fresh R process, and reads back what the knit recorded: the failures, and the arm that each governed span chose. The result says which arms no case reached and which spans no case evaluated, so that a manuscript's wording can be checked for every value its parameters may take (rules 3.7.1 to 3.7.4).

Usage

rehearse(file, cases)

Arguments

file

The path of a .qmd or .Rmd document.

cases

A named list. Each element is a named list of the parameters that case sets (an empty list for the defaults).

Value

An object of class weft_rehearsal, a list:

  • cases: a named list, one element per case, each a list of ok (no failures and the knit finished), error (the message when the knit itself stopped, else NA), failures (the data frame of last_knit()$failures), warnings (the data frame of last_knit()$warnings; ok ignores it) and chosen (a data frame of span, file, line, key, expr, arm, role and text, one row for each governed span the case evaluated; span matches arms(); arm, role and text are NA for a span that was evaluated and chose no arm);

  • arms: arms() of the file (the same object, with its class and errors attribute) with one logical column for each case (did the case choose this arm) and reached (did any);

  • unreached: the rows of arms that no case reached;

  • unevaluated: the rows of the spans that no case evaluated at all (those nested in arms that were never chosen).

Details

Each case is a named list of params. The knit has the document's default parameters with the case's values over them; a name that the document does not declare is an error, raised before anything runs. A default written !r is evaluated in the child process, in the document's folder, and one that cannot be evaluated stops that case with the error. A case cannot be named after a column of the result (file, line, context, span, key, expr, arm, role, text, parent_span, parent_arm or reached). The knit's working directory is the document's, as in a render, for a .qmd too. Draft mode is on, so a case with failures runs to its end; a case whose knit stops is reported in its error and the next case runs.

Nothing is written to the project. The output and the figures go to a temporary directory that is removed, and the child process runs with the environment variable WEFT_REHEARSE=1, which makes weft write no stamp, no collection line, no draft JSON file and no ledger, and use no chunk cache (cache = FALSE is forced for every chunk, wherever its cache was set, so no cache directory appears). A chunk of the document that itself writes files is the author's affair.

Limits

Only knitr::knit() runs: not Pandoc and not Quarto, because a rehearsal needs the records and not the output. Because Quarto does not run, a {{< include >}} is not expanded and project-level metadata is not read; that includes execute-dir, so the working directory is always the document's folder, never the project root. A .qmd whose inline code uses the {r} form is knitted with a stand-in for Quarto's .QuartoInlineRender. A document that reads its data some other way than through its parameters renders the same data in every case (rule 3.7.4).

The child process is started in the project root (the nearest folder upward that holds _weft.yml or _quarto.yml, else the document's folder) and reads that folder's .Rprofile, as a render does, so a document that activates weft there can be rehearsed. It is not run with --vanilla.

Only the spans of the file rehearsed are reported: a span in a document that a chunk includes with child= is not listed or reported. A span that a case evaluates more than once (a weft_str() in a loop) is reported once, with the last arm it chose. A case value is not checked against the default's type, and cases cannot be empty.

The child process loads the same weft as this one: when it was loaded by pkgload (as devtools::load_all() does) from a source directory, the child loads that directory, and otherwise it calls library(weft).
